items.title: The name
items.text: Still PepsiCo’s. It has been used for a sweepstakes of 13,000 six-packs (2015), two summer retail runs at $1.79 a bottle (2016, 2017) and a contest with 300 winners (2022).[^25][^29][^32][^34]

items.title: The original formula
items.text: Withdrawn in 1994 for a citrus cola called Crystal, which carried the line “From the makers of Pepsi.”[^19] We found no record of when that product ended.

items.title: Diet Crystal Pepsi
items.text: PepsiCo said the product would be reintroduced in 1994 “in a nondiet version only.”[^2] It has not been part of any revival we found.

items.title: Tab Clear
items.text: Launched in January 1993 and gone within the year by later accounts.[^11][^21]

items.title: The creator
items.text: David Novak went on to run Yum Brands and has discussed the failure in interviews ever since.[^20][^34]

items.title: The next return
items.text: In September 2026 a food site reported a social media rumor of a return in May 2027, in cans and bottles, and noted that PepsiCo had not confirmed it.[^35] Treat it as unverified.

items.title: The idea
items.text: Fortune noted in 2016 that what ended the original: “Too many me-too products.”[^29] The premise that some drinkers avoid caramel color returned on its own: in 2015 the soda maker Zevia removed coloring from its whole range.[^24]

blocks.title: One owner, six releases
blocks.subtitle: The name was never sold. What changed was how much of it PepsiCo was willing to make.

nodes.what: Test markets in Providence, Dallas and Colorado.[^5]
National launch in regular and diet versions, with an estimated $40 million of advertising.[^8]
Original withdrawn. A citrus reformulation is sold as Crystal, without the Pepsi name.[^2][^19]
Sweepstakes through the Pepsi Pass app.[^25]
Two limited retail runs in the United States, and one in Canada in 2016.[^27][^30][^32]
No Crystal Pepsi on sale that we could confirm. A 2027 return is rumored and unconfirmed.[^35]
